name: HI-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbency in a heavily Democratic state
model.rationale: Hawaii's second district leans heavily Democratic and incumbent Jill Tokuda holds a commanding money edge over Republican Brenton Awa, who has raised little and has minimal cash on hand. Markets price her near-certain to win, and no evidence suggests a competitive race.
model.watch: Any late polling showing Awa gaining traction, or a surge of outside spending against Tokuda, would be the first sign of a real contest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Jill Tokuda seeks a second term in a district that voted about twelve points more Democratic than the nation in recent cycles. She has raised over $820,000 and holds more than $570,000 on hand, while Republican Brenton Awa has raised about $123,000 with little cash remaining and no reported outside support. No general-election polls or expert ratings are available for the race.

Prediction markets give Tokuda roughly a 96 percent chance of winning. With no polling and no outside spending on either side, the forecast rests on the district's partisan lean, incumbency, and the lopsided financial picture, all of which point to a comfortable Democratic hold.
